summary: NYISO moves for the maximum 90-day abeyance of the EL26-69 show cause response, to November 16, 2026, so it can build a section 205 filing through its stakeholder governance process and coordinate with the New York transmission owners.
ask: Issue an order by August 13, 2026 holding the proceeding in abeyance for 90 days until November 16, 2026, with a five-day answer period.

points.point: NYISO requests the full 90 days and action by August 13.
points.quote: hold this proceeding in abeyance for the maximum period permitted by the Show Cause Order, i.e., for 90 days, until November 16, 2026.

points.point: NYISO plans a new large load study process replacing its existing load interconnection rules, with expedited joint studies.
points.quote: the NYISO plans to create a new large load study process that would replace and improve upon its existing load interconnection rules.

points.point: NYISO would offer firm and non-firm variants of its financial reservation service, with non-firm withdrawal service for flexible large loads.
points.quote: make large loads eligible to take non-firm withdrawal service to the extent their ability to be flexible mitigates their impact on the system.

points.point: For co-location, NYISO intends to sunset its BTM:NG program and treat load and generation as separate market entities.
points.quote: the NYISO intends to propose sunsetting its BTM:NG program and replacing it with a new co-located resource participation model

points.point: NYISO ties the timing to New York's shared governance and the NYPSC's parallel large-load proceeding.
points.quote: a 90-day abeyance is reasonable in the NYISO's case because it will facilitate the NYISO's ability to obtain approval from its stakeholder Management Committee before making a section 205 filing.

points.point: Schedule: committee votes October 14 and 15, Management Committee October 28, filing November 16, 2026.
points.quote: Provided that Management Committee and Board approvals are secured, the NYISO will submit a section 205 proposal on November 16, 2026

throughLine.text: Invokes the E-12 order's 90-day abeyance option and describes the section 205 package NYISO plans on study process, flexible service, co-location and proximate generation.
